gloss: Let me explain this with a diagram.
This is called the 20-20-60 split.
The first 20% of people fall into the Never Buy category.
Neither they nor we know why they are here.
They have no need, and they can't pay.
However hard we try to sell, they will definitely not buy.
So our effort on them is a waste of time. They don't need sales.
Another 20% are Definitely Buy.
They are like Amazon shoppers. When we buy something on Amazon,
really buy (not just add to cart), we decide we want it, go look at the product,
search, read the description, check the details and the features,
see it's good, purchase it and leave.
These people are the same. About us, our website, what we sell,
they've checked everything, decided they want us, and come to us as a lead.
So there's no need to work hard selling them the features.
Tell them what it is and the price, and they'll buy. They are Definitely Buy.
But there's another 60% of people. They are the Confused Buyers.
First: do they even need this product? Whom should they buy from?
If they buy it, will they use it?
Do they need it now or in the future? Or something else instead?
They have many confusions like this, and need help making the decision.
Only if someone helps can they decide what they need and what they don't.
This is exactly why sales exists:
to give clarity to the confused and help them decide.

styles.name: Ten People
styles.promise: Out of every ten people, only the six confused ones need a salesperson.
method: Shot board: ID, frame, action, camera, continuity
bible: 10 stickmen on one ground line, 1 figure = 10%
Gray = never buy, black = sure buyer, red = confused
Salesman: black, red tie, always enters/stands screen-right

fields.question: Where are we?
fields.action: Figures walk in left to right and stop on their slots. At 2.4s the three group boxes draw on.

fields.question: Who is the first group?
fields.action: Figures 1-2 turn gray, label drops in
fields.camera: Slow push-in to the left third
fields.continuity: Gray = never buy for the rest of the film

fields.question: Why are they here?
fields.action: All three shrug with ? at the same time
fields.continuity: Salesman intro: black with red tie, label 'us'

fields.question: Can selling change them?
fields.action: Bubbles 'no need' and '₹0' pop on cue 5. Red pitch arrows on cue 6 bounce off, then a red X
fields.continuity: Screen direction: salesman always on the right

fields.question: So what?
fields.action: Sweat drops on the salesman, the word SALES is crossed out on cue 7b

fields.question: Who is the second group?
fields.frame: Wide line again, then laptop inset
fields.action: Figures 3-4 get a bold outline. On cue 9 an 'online shop' laptop appears as an analogy inset

fields.question: What does a sure buyer do?
fields.frame: Over-the-shoulder at laptop, step chips on the right
fields.action: One chip per spoken step, in the order the words are spoken

fields.question: How do they reach us?
fields.frame: Wide: website left, our counter right
fields.action: Buyer walks from the website to the salesman. 'LEAD' tag on cue 14

fields.question: How much selling do they need?
fields.action: Feature list is crossed out. 'What? + price' appear, then a check over the buyer

fields.question: Who is left?
fields.action: Six figures turn red with ? marks
fields.continuity: Red = confused (and later: where sales helps)

fields.question: What confuses them?
fields.action: One thought bubble per question, popping as each is spoken

fields.question: What do they need?
fields.frame: Group left, knot of questions above
fields.action: Bubbles knot together. On cue 22 the salesman walks in from the right

fields.question: So why does sales exist?
fields.action: The knot straightens into a line on cue 24, then the CLARITY label and a check
fields.camera: Slow push-in, end on a hold

styles.name: Living Bar
styles.promise: One 20 | 20 | 60 bar stays on screen the whole time and fills with people as each group is explained.
method: Hierarchy across time: establish → reveal → context → hold
Entry / hold / exit timing per graphic
bible: Bar stays pinned at the top: the orientation anchor
Easing: step-hold for numbers, ease-out for labels
Never more than two jobs per graphic

fields.purpose: Draw an empty bar so the viewer knows a diagram is coming
Snap the three numbers in, left to right, in the order spoken
Label the first group and give it bodies
fields.timing: Fill 0.5s, label ease-out, long hold for reading

fields.purpose: Show the two reasons as two separate pops so neither gets lost
fields.timing: ? at cue 4, two bubbles 1.4s apart on cue 5

fields.purpose: Make wasted effort visible: arrows go in, nothing comes out
fields.timing: Arrows linear in, ease-in fade. SKIP stamp step-hold on cue 7

fields.purpose: Same entrance grammar as segment 1, so the pattern is learnable
Reveal each step exactly as it is spoken, to show they sell to themselves
fields.timing: Each chip 0.3s ease-out on its word, BUY gets a red snap

fields.purpose: Reuse the same chip grammar for our website so the analogy carries over
Contrast: features struck out, two small cards are enough
fields.timing: Strike 0.3s, cards ease-out, check holds to the end

fields.purpose: The biggest segment fills last and fills widest, so size reads as importance
Stack one question per spoken question, to show the pile-up
fields.timing: Each line step-hold on its word, nothing exits

beats.title: Stuck at the fork, help arrives

fields.purpose: A fork plus knot equals can't decide alone. The helper enters on 'only if someone helps'
fields.timing: Fork draw-on, knot wobble, helper walk 0.6s

fields.purpose: Bracket the 60% segment. The knot becomes a straight line on 'clarity'
fields.timing: Arrow ease-out, untie 0.8s ease-in-out, hold to the end

styles.name: Three Doors
styles.promise: After watching, the viewer can sort prospects into three groups and knows which door sales effort belongs behind.
method: Decompose: terms → parts → contrast → example → consequence
Analogy check: what maps / what doesn't / where to stop
bible: Gray = no-go, black = ready, red = confusion and sales help
Analogy 'online shopper': maps research-before-contact; doesn't map marketplace; stops before reviews/discounts

fields.access: Numbers are written, not only colour-coded

fields.learn: Group 1 is called Never Buy, with no clear reason to be here
fields.access: Label sits under the door, high contrast

beats.title: No need, no money, no sale

fields.learn: No need + can't pay = no amount of selling works
fields.grammar: Cause/effect: the pitch goes in, the door shuts
fields.access: The door slam is a soft movement, no flash

fields.learn: Spending sales effort here is waste
fields.grammar: Before/after: the door is X'd out
fields.access: The X is a shape as well as red

beats.title: Door 2: they shop like online buyers

fields.learn: Sure buyers research and decide alone
fields.grammar: Process: numbered chain beside the door
fields.access: Analogy maps: they research before contact. Doesn't map: they're on our site, not a marketplace. Stop: no reviews or discounts implied

beats.title: They come out holding a lead ticket

fields.learn: They arrive already decided, as a lead
fields.grammar: Process: exit through the door toward us
fields.access: LEAD shown as a word, not an icon

fields.learn: Only say what it is and the price
fields.access: Check mark is a shape, not colour only
Each question is short; 4 words max

beats.title: Going in circles, help steps in

fields.learn: They can only decide with help
fields.access: The helper's action is shown, not only described

beats.title: This door is where sales belongs

fields.learn: Sales = clarity for the confused (core takeaway)
fields.access: Final hold of more than 3s for reading

styles.name: Effort Meter
styles.promise: Sales effort only pays off with confused buyers.
method: Arc: problem → stakes → solution → how → payoff
Pacing per beat + VO timing math (2.3 words/s)
bible: Red battery on the salesman = his effort
Battery drains only on gray, flows usefully only to red
Three target boards pinned on top: 20 / 20 / 60

beats.title: Salesman with a full effort battery

fields.why: Introduce the single analogy (effort battery) before the problem
Make the viewer feel the cost: the battery empties for zero
Introduce the sure buyer; battery untouched
Contrast: the buyer sells to themselves while the battery stays full
Effort used here: about 5%. Selling features is unnecessary
Slow down: one bubble per spoken question
The same battery now flows into people who need it: the analogy pays off
Repeatable line: sales = clarity for the confused

styles.name: Whiteboard Teacher
styles.promise: A stickman teacher draws the 20-20-60 pie live, cutting to small doodle scenes for each idea.
method: N: number shots, group by setup
E: edit on paper (stopwatch pass, change every 2–4 s)
bible: Markers: black, red; gray for 'done' text

explored.why: Most literal reading of the percentages; one continuity bible

explored.name: Living Bar
explored.why: Diagrammatic, as the speaker says in cue 1

explored.name: Three Doors
explored.why: Spatial sorting; door size encodes share

explored.name: Effort Meter
explored.why: One analogy makes the 'why sales exists' payoff felt

explored.name: Whiteboard Teacher
explored.why: Matches 'let me explain diagrammatically'; fast visual rhythm

explored.name: Fishing net (cast net over a crowd)
explored.why: Adds a metaphor the speaker never uses, so it leaves the script's context

explored.name: Traffic light (red / amber / green)
explored.why: Needs green and amber, which are outside the palette

explored.name: Amazon checkout screen recreation
explored.why: Uses a real brand's UI and logo; replaced with a generic 'online shop'

explored.why: A funnel implies stages that people move through; the script describes three fixed groups
